<!--
Raw communications corpus for ACC-003 (NovaPower Grid).
Deliberately messy and multi-source: long email threads with quoted history and
signatures, internal Slack, support tickets, and a rambling CRM call note. It
contains noise (an out-of-office), one contradiction (an old chirpy note vs. the
current escalation), and a hearsay competitor mention — so the extraction has to
actually reason, not pattern-match. Do not "clean this up"; the mess is the point.
-->

### [EMAIL | 2026-08-05 | dana.ruiz@novapower.example → sarah.chen@fieldora.com]
Subject: Re: Re: scheduling outage — AGAIN

Sarah,

Frankly, this is unacceptable. The scheduling module went down twice this month,
and this morning it happened again during our 6am dispatch window. My crews were
standing around for forty minutes. I am still waiting on the update you promised
last week.

I have leadership asking me why we are paying for something that keeps failing. I
need a real answer this time, not another "we've escalated it."

> On Aug 1, Sarah Chen wrote:
> Hi Dana — thanks for flagging, we've escalated this to engineering and I'll get
> you an update by end of week.
>
> > On Jul 31, Dana Ruiz wrote:
> > The platform went down again. This is the second time. Please advise.

Dana Ruiz
Director of Grid Operations, NovaPower
—
This message and any attachments are confidential and intended solely for the
addressee. If you have received this in error, please delete it.

### [EMAIL | 2026-08-05 | sarah.chen@fieldora.com → dana.ruiz@novapower.example]
Subject: Re: Re: scheduling outage — AGAIN

Dana — I completely understand the frustration and I'm sorry. I've escalated this
to our engineering lead as a P1 and I'm pushing for a root-cause by Thursday. I'd
like to get our VP of Engineering on a call with you this week. Are you free
Wednesday afternoon?

Sarah

### [EMAIL | 2026-08-06 | noreply@novapower.example → sarah.chen@fieldora.com]
Subject: Automatic reply: Re: scheduling outage — AGAIN

I am out of the office until August 11 with limited access to email. For urgent
grid-operations matters, contact the NOC duty desk. For all other matters I will
respond on my return.

### [SLACK | #cs-novapower | 2026-08-06]
@here heads-up on NovaPower — renewal is in 45 days and this is not in a good spot.
Adoption is stuck around 40% (2 of 5 modules), compliance reporting is still not
working, and Dana is escalating outages to her leadership. I'm setting up an exec
call. Flagging as at-risk for the Monday review.

### [SLACK | #cs-team | 2026-07-30]
btw on NovaPower — heard secondhand from the AE that their team has started looking
at what else is out there for scheduling. Not confirmed, but worth taking seriously
given the renewal timing.

### [SUPPORT | TKT-847 | open 12d | priority: high]
Subject: Platform performance degradation during peak scheduling
Customer reports the scheduling module becomes unresponsive during the 6am dispatch
window. Reproduced intermittently. Two related outages logged this month. Awaiting
root-cause from engineering. Customer has asked for status twice.

### [SUPPORT | TKT-851 | open 5d]
Subject: Compliance report export failing
The monthly compliance report export returns an error for this account. Customer
notes they have a regulatory filing due and "the compliance reporting is still not
working." Escalated to the reporting team.

### [CRM_NOTE | QBR call log | 2026-07-17 | attendees: D.Ruiz, new VP Ops M.Feld, S.Chen]
QBR recap. Tone was tense. Dana was direct: "we need to see this stabilize before we
commit to the renewal." A new VP of Operations, Marcus Feld, has joined on their
side and is reviewing all vendor contracts. Core scheduling is live but the crews
don't trust it after the outages; compliance reporting has been delayed for two
months. Action items: root-cause the outages, get compliance export working, and
schedule an exec-to-exec call before renewal.
(For contrast: my Q1 note on this account read "relationship is healthy, champion
very engaged" — that has clearly changed since the outages started.)
